advisories.title: Unauthenticated DoS: integer user API public key triggers RSA key generation
advisories.summary:
Passing an integer to `OpenSSL::PKey::RSA.new` generates a new RSA keypair of that bit length rather than parsing an existing key. Several endpoints fed the unvalidated `public_key` request param straight into this call, so an unauthenticated attacker could send a large integer (e.g. a multi-kilobit "key") and force the server to spend seconds generating a keypair per request, tying up Puma workers and degrading or denying service.

The most severe path was `ApplicationController#redirect_to_login_if_required`, which handled `user_api_public_key` on anonymous requests with no rate limiting. The user API key client creation endpoint and the device auth flow had the same pattern.

### Workarounds

None. Sites can mitigate by rate-limiting unauthenticated requests at the proxy, but the vulnerable paths ran before rate limiting on the worst endpoint.

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerability ANT-2026-DJF9HY4Q.

advisories.title: QuoteComparer skips Guardian: any user can read PMs via quote-modified
advisories.summary:
### Impact
Information disclosure. When a post containing a `[quote]` is cooked, Discourse compares the quoted text against the original post and marks the block with a `quote-modified` or `quote-post-not-found` CSS class. This comparison loaded the parent post by topic id and post number with no Guardian check, so the result reflected posts the quoting user cannot see.

Any logged-in user could post a quote targeting an arbitrary topic id and post number, including private messages and posts in restricted categories.

### Patches
incoming

### Workarounds
none

advisories.title: Markdown root route leaks Latest topic list on login_required sites
advisories.summary:
### Impact
Discourse contains an authentication bypass affecting login-required sites with Markdown endpoints enabled.

### Patches


### Workarounds
Disable the feature via the `enable_markdown_endpoints` site setting. 


Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerability ANT-2026-GPGS4NF7.

advisories.title: Denial of Service via Unbounded Search Terms
advisories.summary:
### Impact
A denial-of-service vulnerability existed in Discourse's full-text search implementation. The search functionality accepted unbounded input terms, which were passed directly to the underlying database's ranking functions. An attacker could craft a search query combined with specific content patterns to cause excessive CPU consumption on the database and application servers, potentially rendering the site unresponsive.

This issue affects sites where the search feature is enabled (enabled by default). No authentication is required to trigger the vulnerability, although existing rate limits may mitigate the frequency of such attacks.

### Workarounds
No known workarounds for this issue

<!-- patch-triage-lifecycle:05f6b8aece9ac562693d76eadad66624f7ec3b0b53e83df608943d18be598428 -->

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerability ANT-2026-B2HVFQ0W.

advisories.title: ReDoS in Markdown Image Size Parsing
advisories.summary:
### Impact
A Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) vulnerability existed in the Markdown parser used by Discourse. Specifically, the regular expression responsible for parsing image size suffixes in Markdown syntax contained ambiguous quantifiers that resulted in catastrophic backtracking when processing certain malformed numeric inputs.

An attacker with a Trust Level of 0 or higher (any registered user who can create posts or reply) could exploit this by submitting a post containing a specifically crafted Markdown image tag with long, invalid numeric dimensions. This caused the server-side Markdown rendering process ("cooking") to consume excessive CPU resources for an extended period. Due to internal locking mechanisms during the cooking process, a single malicious request could block all other Markdown rendering operations on the worker, leading to significant performance degradation or temporary site-wide availability issues affecting post creation, edits, and chat messages. There is no impact on data confidentiality or integrity; the malicious input is treated as literal text.

### Workarounds
Site administrators can mitigate this issue by deploying a Web Application Firewall (WAF) rule that inspects incoming post bodies for Markdown image syntax (`![...`) containing excessively long sequences of digits in the size suffix attribute (e.g., `![alt|...x...]`). Blocking requests where the size attribute contains more than a few hundred consecutive characters before processing can prevent the regex backtracking. Additionally, strictly enforcing rate limits on post creation may reduce the effectiveness of concurrent attempts to exhaust server resources.

<!-- patch-triage-lifecycle:900bb76fa6b1ad21adcd3e9cc3738ea7b2597830fcfd29a3ae06111a2c2284ae -->

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerability ANT-2026-FT274P2I.

advisories.title: Restricted category Chat messages disclosed to readonly members via MessageBus
advisories.summary:
### Impact
Users with only "See" permission on a restricted category could receive new chat messages from that category's chat channel in real time, even though they are not allowed to join the channel or read its history.

This only affects sites with a chat channel on a restricted category where at least one group has "See" permission without "Reply" or "Create". It does not allow posting, moderation, or access to earlier messages.

### Workarounds
Remove "See"-only groups from the security settings of restricted categories that have a chat channel.

advisories.title: Cross-group authorization bypass in group inbox email replies
advisories.summary:
### Impact
An authorization bypass in group inbox email processing could allow an external sender to be added to, read, and reply to a private group conversation belonging to a different group.

This only affects sites where the `email in` site setting is enabled and at least one group with an incoming email address has "Allow unknown sender topic replies" enabled. This is not the default.

### Workarounds
Disable "Allow unknown sender topic replies" (group page > Manage > Email) on every group that has it enabled. Replies from unknown senders to those groups will then create new topics instead.

advisories.title: Inactive account profiles disclosed through bulk user card lookup
advisories.summary:
### Impact

Discourse shows non-staff users only a minimal profile card for inactive accounts, such as deactivated accounts and staged accounts. A bulk user card lookup did not apply this rule. Anyone who can view user profiles could see the full card of inactive accounts, including the bio, location, website and other card details, and could collect them in bulk without knowing their usernames. On sites that let the public view user profiles, which is the default, anonymous visitors can do this.

### Patches

Fixed in 2026.11.0-latest.1, 2026.10.1, 2026.9.2 and 2026.7.5.

### Workarounds

Enabling the `hide user profiles from public` site setting stops anonymous visitors from exploiting this, at the cost of hiding every user profile from anonymous visitors. Logged-in users who are not staff can still see the affected cards.

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerability ANT-2026-FIHVE9B0.

advisories.title: Hidden tag names disclosed through bulk topic actions
advisories.summary:
### Impact

Users who can edit a topic could learn the names of tags on that topic that are hidden from them, such as staff-only tags.

This affects sites with tagging enabled that use tag groups to hide tags from some users and limit which tags can be used in each category. Only tag names are disclosed. Topic content and permissions are not affected.

### Patches

Fixed in 2026.11.0-latest.1, 2026.10.1, 2026.9.2, 2026.7.5.

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerability ANT-2026-6WJ8381O.

advisories.title: HTML injection in oneboxes via external page metadata
advisories.summary:
### Impact

Oneboxes display metadata from the linked page, such as its title, description or image size. Several onebox renderers inserted these values into HTML without escaping them, so a user who posts a link to a page they control could inject HTML into the onebox stored in their post. That HTML is shown to everyone who views the post, and can be styled, for example to cover the page with fake content. Scripts are still removed.

The same applies to some site-specific oneboxes when the uploader controls the title or text, for example X/Twitter and Threads posts or Flickr, Imgur and Google Photos albums.

### Patches

External metadata is now escaped in all onebox renderers. Fixed in `2026.11.0-latest`. Fixed release versions will be added after the fix and backports are released.

Posts cooked before the fix keep the injected HTML until they are rebaked.

### Workarounds

Set `max_oneboxes_per_post` to `0` to stop new posts from getting oneboxes. Existing posts are not affected by the setting.

### References

None.

advisories.title: HTML injection in personal message notification emails via participant names
advisories.summary:
### Impact

Notification emails for personal messages list the other participants as links. User and group names were inserted into these emails without sanitization, so a name containing HTML or Markdown was rendered as markup in the emails other participants receive, for example to add images, restyle the email or insert misleading links.

A group full name can be set by group owners, so this works with default settings for any group that is invited to a personal message. A user's own full name is only used when `prioritize_username_in_ux` is disabled. Sites where an admin customized the email header, footer or preview text to include `%{topic_title}` were also affected through topic titles.

### Patches

The email snippets are now sanitized and participant names are escaped. Fixed in `2026.11.0-latest`. Fixed release versions will be added after the fix and backports are released.

### Workarounds

Keep `prioritize_username_in_ux` enabled, and avoid `%{topic_title}` in customized email header, footer or preview texts. There is no workaround for group full names other than reviewing the full names of groups with non-staff owners.

### References

None.

advisories.title: HTML injection in notification emails via iframe URLs and secure image sizes
advisories.summary:
### Impact

When rendering notification emails, Discourse converts embedded iframes into links and inlines images from secure uploads. Both were built by inserting post content into HTML strings. A user could craft a post so that the notification emails other users receive for it contained injected HTML attributes, for example to restyle the email or disguise a link.

The iframe case requires the iframe's origin to be allowed by the `allowed_iframes` site setting. The image case requires secure uploads with `secure_uploads_allow_embed_images_in_emails` enabled.

### Patches

The link and image are now built as HTML nodes, and image dimensions must be numeric. Fixed in `2026.11.0-latest`. Fixed release versions will be added after the fix and backports are released.

### Workarounds

Disable `secure_uploads_allow_embed_images_in_emails` to mitigate the image case. For the iframe case, remove unneeded origins from `allowed_iframes`; this disables those embeds in posts.

### References

None.

advisories.title: HTML injection via Unicode bidirectional characters in code blocks
advisories.summary:
### Impact

Discourse highlights hidden Unicode bidirectional characters in code blocks so readers can see them. The highlighting step parsed the post's HTML again, so a user could craft a post where an attribute value containing these characters turned back into HTML, bypassing the sanitizer. This could be used to inject arbitrary HTML into posts. The default Content Security Policy blocks script execution from the injected markup.

This is only exploitable with Nokogiri 1.19.4 and earlier, which do not escape `<` and `>` in attribute values. Supported releases bundle Nokogiri 1.19.7 and are not known to be exploitable; on them, the issue only corrupts such attribute values.

### Patches

The highlighting now rewrites text nodes only and builds the warning markup as nodes, so no HTML is parsed again. Fixed in `2026.11.0-latest`. Fixed release versions will be added after the fix and backports are released.

### Workarounds

No known workarounds for the HTML injection. Keep the default Content Security Policy enabled to prevent script execution.

### References

- https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2021-42574

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerability ANT-2026-7X9UVRAT.

advisories.title: Censored watched words can inject HTML attributes into quoted chat messages
advisories.summary:
### Impact

On sites that use censored watched words containing a wildcard (`*`), a user could craft a chat transcript (a quote of chat messages) so that censoring rewrote HTML that had already passed the sanitizer. This let the user inject HTML attributes and elements that the sanitizer would have removed, which could be used for content spoofing or to overlay parts of the page. The default Content Security Policy blocks script execution from the injected markup.

Only sites with the Chat plugin enabled and at least one censored watched word that uses a wildcard are affected.

### Patches

The censor no longer rewrites HTML that is restored after sanitization. Fixed in `2026.11.0-latest`. Fixed release versions will be added after the fix and backports are released.

### Workarounds

Remove the wildcard (`*`) from censored watched words, or delete those watched words, until a patched version is available.

### References

None.

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerability ANT-2026-1KUBK80U.

advisories.title: Discourse AI retries can access private content using another user's permissions
advisories.summary:
### Impact

A user allowed to use the AI bot could retry a response to another user's prompt and cause agent tools to run with the original prompt author's permissions.

When the original author had access to private content, configured tools could retrieve that content or copy private artifacts into a conversation visible to the retrying user.

Exploitation requires a shared conversation, an eligible retrying user, and the model selecting an affected tool. Unauthorized private reads and artifact imports were reproduced with request-level regression tests. Integrity impact has not been demonstrated.

### Patches

A fix is prepared. Patched release versions have not yet been established.

### Workarounds

Disable the AI bot to prevent new retry requests until the fix is deployed.

advisories.title: Two factor authentication bypass during account activation
advisories.summary:
### Impact

An attacker who knows a deactivated account’s password could bypass configured two factor authentication and gain access to that account. Administrator accounts are affected, so successful exploitation could compromise the site.

### Patches

This issue is patched in the latest version of Discourse.

### Workarounds

None.

advisories.title: Topic publishing lets non-staff users expose restricted topics and erase edit history
advisories.summary:
### Impact

Publishing a topic moves it to another category, relists it, resets its dates and permanently deletes the opening post's edit history. Some non-staff users could publish topics they were not allowed to edit:

- On sites that add non-staff groups to `shared_drafts_allowed_groups`, a member of such a group could publish any topic they could read, not only shared drafts. A member who could edit a topic could also turn it into a shared draft, which hid it from everyone outside the group.
- Users allowed to set topic timers, which by default includes trust level 4 users, could schedule a topic they could only read to be published into another category.

In both cases, a topic from a read-restricted category could be moved into a public category and become readable by anyone.

### Workarounds

Remove non-staff groups from the `shared_drafts_allowed_groups` site setting, and remove trust level 4 from the `topic_timers_allowed_groups` site setting.

<!-- patch-triage-lifecycle:7caf7e69f8fece8381d80a21e0756912f5ccdca32f17f69858f28c2143283bb2 -->

advisories.title: Deleted whispers visible to moderators outside whisper-allowed groups
advisories.summary:
### Impact

On sites that restrict whispers to specific groups, moderators who are not members of any group in `whispers_allowed_groups` could read deleted whispers through a user's deleted posts list. 

### Workarounds

No known workarounds that keep whispers hidden from moderators. Sites that intend moderators to see whispers can add them to a group in `whispers_allowed_groups`.

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerability ANT-2026-0EQDJQOX.

advisories.title: Unauthorized group membership via user field automation
advisories.summary:
# Impact

In the bundled Automation plugin, the "Add user to group through User Custom Field" script adds a user to a group selected by the value of a user field. When the script used a free-text user field, a user could make it select an automatic group, such as admins or moderators. Any person who can create an account could do this.

With the default settings, membership in these groups lets the user edit other users' posts, delete topics, and read content restricted to these groups. The user does not get the admin or moderator role, and cannot open the admin interface.

Only sites that enabled the Automation plugin and configured this script on a free-text user field are affected.

# Workarounds
- Disable the automation, or
- Change the user field that the automation uses to a dropdown.

To find affected accounts, examine the group logs of the automatic groups for members that the system user added.

# After the update

The script no longer adds users to automatic groups. It can still add users to any other group that has a full name, so use it with a free-text field only for groups that any user may join.

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerability ANT-2026-6JM1BR5X.

advisories.title: Template injection in Automation placeholders lets any user become admin
advisories.summary:
### Impact

On sites with the Automation plugin enabled, an automation that inserts user-written text using the `%%KEY%%` placeholder syntax (for example `%%TOPIC_TITLE%%`, `%%POST_QUOTE%%`, or a user's name or profile field) evaluated any template tags contained in that text on the server. A user of any trust level could craft a topic title or post that, once processed by such an automation, grants them admin privileges, reads server secrets such as the secret key base, or reads other users' data such as e-mail addresses. `%%REPORT=…%%` placeholders were affected in the same way when the report lists user-written text (for example search terms).

Automation templates that only use the `{{key}}` placeholder syntax are not affected. The Automation plugin is disabled by default.

Admin privileges granted this way are not recorded in the staff action logs. Administrators of affected sites should review their list of admins for unexpected accounts.

### Patches

Placeholder values are now always inserted as plain text and are never evaluated as template code. Templates can now only look up placeholder values, so dotted method access such as `{{topic_title.length}}` renders as an empty string. Fixed release versions will be added after the fix and backports are released.

### Workarounds

Disable the Automation plugin (`discourse_automation_enabled`), or edit automations so that templates use `{{key}}` instead of `%%KEY%%` for user-written values and do not use `%%REPORT=…%%` with reports that list user-written text.

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerability ANT-2026-0WFNSUZI.

advisories.title: Automation trigger endpoint allows forged event context to disclose private post content
advisories.summary:
### Impact

A vulnerability exists in the automation trigger endpoint (`POST /automations/:id/trigger.json`) that could allow disclosure of private post content. An attacker with a granular API key scoped only to `automation:trigger_automation` could invoke automations that are configured for event-only triggering (such as the flagged-post email notification workflow). By supplying forged event context, the attacker could cause the automation to process data referencing private posts, potentially leading to disclosure of post excerpts to unauthorized recipients.

The issue is limited by several preconditions: the attacker must possess a valid API key bound to an administrator account with the `automation:trigger_automation` scope, know the automation ID, and be able to supply a valid action ID referencing a private post. The granular key alone does not provide direct access to private topics or posts.

Only confidentiality is affected; there is no impact on data integrity (no posts or topics are modified) or availability.

### Workarounds

No known workarounds for this issue.

<!-- patch-triage-lifecycle:0c42bb79579ede228fd909e86e34bd5f82cc0745d4ca402c93dfd46c08f6d3d3 -->

advisories.title: Arbitrary file read via newlines in upload file names during S3 migration
advisories.summary:
### Impact
When a crafted backup is restored on a site using S3, its upload file names can make Discourse upload files from outside the uploads directory to the bucket, including configuration files. Only sites with `allow_restore` enabled are affected.

### Workarounds
Keep `allow_restore` disabled, and only restore backups from trusted sources.

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerability ANT-2026-4U20ZJW5.

advisories.title: Command injection in the uploads:gather rake task
advisories.summary:
### Impact
Upload records restored from a crafted backup can run shell commands when a sysadmin runs the `uploads:gather` rake task.

### Workarounds
Do not run `uploads:gather` on a database restored from an untrusted backup.

advisories.title: Animated GIF detection reads files outside the store
advisories.summary:
### Impact
Upload records restored from a crafted backup can make the animated GIF detection job read arbitrary URLs without the usual SSRF protections. Only sites with `allow_restore` enabled are affected.

### Workarounds
Keep `allow_restore` disabled, and only restore backups from trusted sources.

advisories.title: External upload stubs can reference files outside the temporary upload folder
advisories.summary:
### Impact
External upload records restored from a crafted backup can make Discourse copy or delete files outside the temporary upload folder in the S3 bucket, including files of other sites sharing that bucket. Only sites using direct S3 uploads with `allow_restore` enabled are affected.

### Workarounds
Keep `allow_restore` disabled, and only restore backups from trusted sources.

advisories.title: Secure uploads of other multisite sites can be signed
advisories.summary:
### Impact
On multisite clusters that share one S3 bucket, an admin of one site can download secure uploads that belong to another site. Single-site installs are not affected.

### Workarounds
Keep `allow_restore` disabled, and only restore backups from trusted sources.


Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerability ANT-2026-ULA08OOG.

advisories.title: Disk caches shared between multisite sites
advisories.summary:
### Impact
On multisite clusters, some disk caches are shared by all sites. An admin of one site can make another site serve content they control, including theme JavaScript. Single-site installs are not affected.

### Workarounds
None.

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerabilities ANT-2026-Z77B3W8H and ANT-2026-JXSIZFSU.

advisories.title: Path traversal in custom emoji export
advisories.summary:
### Impact
Custom emoji names restored from a crafted backup can make the emoji export write files outside its temporary directory. Only sites with `allow_restore` enabled are affected.

### Workarounds
Keep `allow_restore` disabled, and only restore backups from trusted sources.

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerability ANT-2026-UWH9VBAK.

advisories.title: Path traversal in upload file paths from restored backups
advisories.summary:
### Impact
Upload records restored from a crafted backup can point outside the uploads directory. Discourse then reads or writes files elsewhere on the server, including configuration files. Only sites with `allow_restore` enabled are affected.

### Workarounds
Keep `allow_restore` disabled, and only restore backups from trusted sources.

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerabilities ANT-2026-1JDG572G and ANT-2026-4E9WJ0YN.

advisories.title: Backup restore follows symlinks in uploaded archives
advisories.summary:
### Impact
An admin restoring a crafted backup can read and write files outside the restore directory, as the user running Discourse. This can lead to code execution on the server. Only sites with `allow_restore` enabled are affected.

### Workarounds
Keep `allow_restore` disabled, and only restore backups from trusted sources.

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerability ANT-2026-AWV304MJ.

advisories.title: Moving post can leak topic info
advisories.summary:
### Impact

When posts were moved into a topic in a read-restricted category, either by merging them into an existing topic or by splitting them into a new one, the notice left in the original topic included the destination topic's title and a link containing its slug and ID. Any user able to read the original topic, including anonymous visitors when that topic is public, could learn the title of a topic they are not allowed to see.

Moving posts requires a staff member or a user with permission to move posts, so the disclosure only happens as a side effect of their action. The contents of the destination topic are not exposed. All versions of Discourse are affected; the notice has included the destination title since posts could first be moved.

The fix omits the destination title and link from the notice unless every user who can read the original topic can also read the destination. Notices created before upgrading are not changed.

### Workarounds

Avoid moving posts from less restricted topics into topics in read-restricted categories. Existing move notices that reference restricted topics can be deleted by staff.

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerability ANT-2026-XI1ORQA2.

advisories.title: Hidden post content may be exposed in RSS feeds, metadata, and digest emails
advisories.summary:
### Impact

Posts hidden by community flags or staff action could be disclosed to people who were not permitted to view them.

An anonymous visitor with a topic URL could read the full raw body of a hidden first post in the topic RSS feed’s channel description. The topic’s HTML description and Open Graph and Twitter metadata could also expose excerpts from a hidden first or requested post, including when a visitor requested a visible reply. Separately, digest emails could include an excerpt from a hidden reply selected as the topic’s highest-scored post.

In a default configuration, hidden posts are visible to their authors, staff, and trust level 4 users. This issue allowed anonymous visitors and ordinary users to obtain content they should not have been able to read. It did not allow modification of posts or escalation of privileges

### Workarounds

No known complete workaround is available. Updating to a fixed version is recommended.

advisories.title: Privilege Escalation via Scoped API Keys Allowing External Identity Modification
advisories.summary:
### Impact
A granular API key authenticated as an administrator and granted users:update could submit external_ids when updating a user. Although the key was limited to user-update operations, the endpoint could use that parameter to change the user’s DiscourseConnect or managed authentication association. If an attacker controlled the replacement external identity, they could subsequently authenticate as the affected user. Rebinding an administrator account could give the attacker full administrator access.

Exploitation requires a valid scoped key that can update the target user and an applicable external login provider. The users:create endpoint also accepted external_ids and could reassign an existing managed-provider association; its impact should be described separately.

### Workarounds
Until patched, revoke or rotate granular API keys with users:update or users:create access that are held by untrusted integrations. Review restrictions on the users those keys can affect, and inspect external login associations for unexpected changes. If an integration requires these scopes, avoid giving it access to administrator accounts where possible.

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerability ANT-2026-DPIDQ0FE.

advisories.title: Moderator can expose secure uploads via avatar settings
advisories.summary:
### Impact
A privilege escalation and information disclosure vulnerability existed in the user avatar management system. A moderator (a staff user with moderation capabilities) could potentially expose a secure private upload belonging to another user by setting it as that user's avatar. 

Secure uploads (such as images attached to Private Messages or topics restricted from public view) are protected by access controls that prevent unauthorized users from viewing them directly. However, the avatar management endpoint did not adequately verify if the acting moderator had permission to *view* a specific upload before allowing them to *set* it as another user's avatar. 

If a moderator set a secure upload (owned by the target user but restricted from the moderator's view) as the target's avatar, the content could become accessible via the public avatar route (`/user_avatar/...`). This bypassed standard security checks, effectively leaking private content to anyone who could access the user's profile or avatar URL. This vulnerability requires an attacker to have Moderator privileges or higher.

### Workarounds
No known workarounds for this issue.

<!-- patch-triage-lifecycle:4e6497fdfc0f2b41a67107082d96e45ead8ee57443d53ac0439aea658babbef8 -->

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerability ANT-2026-RE0M74BN.

advisories.title: Path traversal in report CSV export
advisories.summary:
### Impact

A path traversal in the report CSV export allows staff users (moderators and admins) to create directories, each containing a small CSV file, anywhere the Discourse process can write on the server.  A directory planted in the plugins folder causes every Discourse process started afterwards to fail during boot.

The issue does not allow code execution, reading files, or overwriting existing files. Regular users cannot exploit it.

All versions since v2.0.0.beta8 are affected. The directory creation that leads to the boot failure was introduced in v2.5.0.beta4.

### Patches

The issue is patched in the latest version of Discourse.

### Workarounds

- Only grant moderator and admin roles to trusted users.
- Check for directories already planted in the plugins folder, and remove any incorrect entry.

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerability ANT-2026-4ADFPFMQ.

advisories.title: oauth2-basic callback paths call Ruby methods
advisories.summary:
### Impact

A site administrator can misuse OAuth2 callback path settings to read server secrets, environment variables, and files, and invoke Ruby methods with side effects.

Hosted and multisite installations are impacted where site administrators do not control the server. Exploitation requires a full administrator account. The bundled plugin is disabled by default.

### Patches

The fix limits callback paths to reading token-response data.

Users should upgrade to patched versions.

### Workarounds

Server operators can apply the patch manually or disable the plugin at the deployment level. Turning it off in site settings is insufficient because an administrator can re-enable it.

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerability ANT-2026-QLGMPQRV.

advisories.title: Race condition in email-code activation allows privilege escalation via address swap
advisories.summary:
### Impact

Discourse sites allowing passwordless login or email-code activation are susceptible to a race condition that could allow an attacker to claim account privileges associated with an email address they do not own.

### Workarounds

Disable the "Enable local logins via code" upcoming change.

<!-- patch-triage-lifecycle:7fb45bff786cae3cc39d950d7b7808100b7d1593583efa58b0d2d04b8f1bccd6 -->

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerability ANT-2026-L95YKBZU.

advisories.title: Admin takeover via user_api_keys
advisories.summary:
### Impact
A vulnerability exists in the User API Key device authorization flow in Discourse. An authenticated user with permission to create user API keys (by default, this includes Trust Level 0 users on sites with open registration) could exploit a parameter handling flaw to authorize a device key for a different user account. The resulting key grants the attacker the same access and privileges as the victim, leading to potential data exposure and unauthorized actions within the application.

### Workarounds
No known workarounds for this issue

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerability ANT-2026-2RCWW0D2.

advisories.title: Staff-initiated DoS via regular expressions
advisories.summary:
Specially crafted regular expressions could lead to memory corruption in the server. This could lead to Denial of Service, and could potentially be escalated to RCE. For more information, see https://www.ruby-lang.org/en/news/2026/10/23/regexp-fixes-for-gitlab-cves/

In Discourse, this is exploitable only by admin/moderator users. Therefore, this security advisory is primarily a concern for shared-hosting environments where admins may not be trusted.

This is resolved by a Ruby patch, which is available in `discourse/base:2.0.20261022-1808` and later. On a standard install, run `./launcher rebuild app` to get the latest version. Web-based updates will be unavailable until this rebuild has been completed.

advisories.title: Free Patreon members may gain access to All Patrons-restricted groups
advisories.summary:
### Impact                                                                   

Sites using the discourse-patreon plugin with API v2 credentials could grant group membership to free Patreon members who are not entitled to patron benefits.

This affects sites where a Discourse group is mapped to the virtual "All Patrons" reward. If that group grants access to restricted content, affected members could read that content, including private categories and topics.
                                                                             
### Workarounds                                                              

Until the fix is applied, administrators can remove the affected groups’ permissions to private content. Access for legitimate patrons can instead be granted through a separate group whose membership is managed manually.

Disabling the Patreon plugin alone does not revoke group memberships already granted.

advisories.title: SSRF through disallowed ports in onebox fetches
advisories.summary:
### Impact

`Onebox::Helpers.fetch_response` checked the resolved IP address but did not apply URL and port restrictions before making a request. On sites with allowlisted internal hosts, a user who can trigger a onebox preview could cause a onebox engine to request an otherwise disallowed port on one of those hosts, directly or through a redirect. Depending on the response and engine, data from that service may appear in the preview. The reported oEmbed case demonstrated metadata appearing in the response.

### Patches

The fix validates each URL and redirect destination in the shared onebox fetch helper before requesting it. Fixed release versions will be added after the fix and backports are released.

### Workarounds

Where possible, remove unnecessary internal hostnames from `allowed_internal_hosts` until a patched version is available. This may interrupt integrations that depend on those hosts.

advisories.title: Category chat reviewables visible to moderators without category access
advisories.summary:
### Impact

Users with moderator review-queue access on a Discourse site with the Chat plugin enabled could, under certain conditions, view flagged chat messages from category channels whose categories they are not permitted to read. Specifically, a moderator excluded from a read-restricted category could retrieve flagged messages (including serialized uploads associated with those messages) from that category's chat channel through the review queue, even though they could not access the channel through normal chat interfaces.

This issue affects sites that have Chat enabled and have category chat channels restricted to a subset of users. The disclosure requires the cooperation of a user with access to the restricted category who flags a message in that channel. The category-channel disclosure is limited to chat reviewables; direct-message reviewables are not affected and remain subject to existing moderator review policy. Administrative users remain trusted and are not subject to this restriction.

### Workarounds

No known workarounds for this issue.

advisories.title: Close MCP private-message read-scope gaps
advisories.summary:
### MCP notification-list tool leaks group private-message summary metadata without required scope

## Impact

A vulnerability in the MCP notification-list tool allows OAuth clients that hold only the `mcp:content:read` scope to retrieve topic-less group private-message summary notifications. These notifications contain sensitive metadata, including the group name, group ID, and unread/inbox count, for the consenting user's group inboxes.

The disclosure is limited to this metadata - no private-message content, topic text, or cross-user data is exposed. The vulnerability affects sites where MCP is enabled and where a group private-message participant authorizes an OAuth MCP client with only content-read scope. No staff privileges, cross-user access, or private-message content access is required.

This is a scoped-access boundary issue: the dedicated `mcp:private-messages:read` scope is required to access private-message-related content, and the notification-list tool already excludes private-message-topic notifications without that scope. The topic-less group summary notifications bypassed that boundary.

## Workarounds

No known workarounds for this issue. MCP is disabled by default and requires site-level enablement; sites that do not enable MCP are not affected.

### MCP draft tool may disclose private-message draft after topic is soft-deleted

### Impact

The Discourse MCP server's `discourse_get_draft` tool could return the content of a retained private-message reply draft to an OAuth client that was not granted the `mcp:private-messages:read` scope, when the private-message topic had been soft-deleted. A draft associated with a live private-message topic was properly protected, but soft-deleted private-message topics were misclassified as non-private because the deleted row was not visible through the topic lookups used for classification. As a result, an OAuth client with only draft-read access could retrieve the user's retained private reply draft via the MCP interface.

This issue affects Discourse installations that have the MCP server feature enabled. Exploitation requires a legitimate OAuth authorization for the affected user that includes draft-read access but explicitly excludes private-message read access, plus a retained private-message reply draft and a soft-deleted private-message topic. Draft lookups remain scoped to the authorized user, so the flaw does not expose other users' drafts. Confidentiality is the only impacted security property; there is no effect on integrity or availability.

### Workarounds

No known workarounds for this issue.

### Calendar MCP tool discloses private-message event metadata without required scope

### Impact

A vulnerability in the Discourse Calendar plugin's Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration allowed clients holding only the `discourse-calendar:read` scope to retrieve metadata about events posted in private-message topics. This violated the platform's MCP scope boundary, which requires the separate `mcp:private-messages:read` scope before returning private-message-derived content to delegated clients.

Affected clients could learn of the existence of private-message calendar events (including event names and timing details) without the proper authorization. Public events were not affected, and private-message content outside of calendar event metadata was not exposed.

The issue affects sites with both the Discourse Events/Calendar plugin and the MCP server enabled, where clients are authenticated via MCP OAuth tokens scoped to `discourse-calendar:read` only.

### Workarounds

No known workarounds for this issue. Site administrators should ensure that MCP clients are only issued to trusted parties and that client access is revoked until the patched version is deployed.

advisories.title: Discourse: Stored oEmbed HTML injection via allowed iframe
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.9.0, 2026.8.1, 2026.7.3, and 2026.1.9, oEmbed processing treated an entire attacker-controlled HTML fragment as trusted when the fragment contained an iframe whose source matched the configured allowlist. A user with posting permission who controlled a public webpage and its oEmbed response could combine an allowlisted iframe with unrelated sibling HTML or CSS, causing stored visual overlays or other styled content to appear in post content and enabling misleading or fraudulent user interfaces. Exploitation requires a posting account, control of the fetched webpage and oEmbed response, and an allowlisted iframe source. The issue affects content integrity but does not expose restricted data, disrupt availability, or require interaction with Discourse Content Security Policy. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.9.0, 2026.8.1, 2026.7.3, and 2026.1.9.

advisories.title: Discourse: Media uploads remain publicly accessible after category permissions are restricted
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.9.0, 2026.8.1, 2026.7.3, and 2026.1.9, sites with secure uploads enabled did not reconcile existing upload security metadata when a previously public category became read-restricted or when category permissions changed during a bulk import. Media and attachments uploaded while the category was public retained a public accessibility flag and remained reachable by anonymous users through their short upload URLs, including uploads associated with deleted topics. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.9.0, 2026.8.1, 2026.7.3, and 2026.1.9.

advisories.title: Discourse: Chat MessageBus delivers read-restricted messages to unauthorized users
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.9.0, 2026.8.1, 2026.7.3, and 2026.1.9, MessageBus audience calculation could deliver messages from a read-restricted category chat channel to an authenticated user who could view the category but was not allowed to use Chat under the site's group restrictions. The publication path bounded events by category visibility without also enforcing Chat eligibility, exposing live and recent message content available in the MessageBus backlog. The issue does not permit retrieval of the channel's full history through the Chat API and does not permit message creation or modification. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.9.0, 2026.8.1, 2026.7.3, and 2026.1.9.

advisories.title: Discourse: Stored HTML injection in video notification emails
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.1.8, 2026.6.3, 2026.7.2, and 2026.8.0, provider-controlled video titles in lazy video embeds could be reparsed as HTML when Discourse generated notification emails or chat summaries. A user with standard posting privileges could create a post for an enabled YouTube, Vimeo, or TikTok provider whose title contained markup, and the email and chat-summary rendering path would place that markup into the output instead of treating it solely as text. Recipients using HTML-capable email clients could see injected content, potentially including event handlers, but the issue did not directly expose a Discourse browser session or affect the forum page itself. Lazy video embeds must be enabled, which is the default configuration. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.1.8, 2026.6.3, 2026.7.2, and 2026.8.0.

advisories.title: Discourse: Chat MessageBus delivers read-restricted messages to unauthorized users
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.1.8, 2026.6.3, 2026.7.2, and 2026.8.0, the video placeholder component allowed crafted HTML to cause an attribute breakout and inject an attacker-controlled event handler. An authenticated user with default trust-level posting privileges could store the crafted placeholder in a post. When another user opened the post and clicked the video play overlay, the handler could execute arbitrary JavaScript in the viewer's session. Default Content Security Policy settings block inline event handlers, but instances with CSP disabled or relaxed could allow the script to read page content and make authenticated requests as the viewer. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.1.8, 2026.6.3, 2026.7.2, and 2026.8.0.

advisories.title: Discourse: Chat upload filenames rendered as raw HTML in excerpts
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.1.8, 2026.6.3, 2026.7.2, and 2026.8.0, attacker-controlled upload filenames used in chat message excerpts were rendered as unescaped HTML. A user able to upload a file and send chat content could place markup in a filename that was then interpreted by chat channel lists, chat summary emails, pinned message bars, reply previews, thread previews, and other excerpt renderers. The issue allowed trusted-HTML injection that altered rendered excerpt content, but JavaScript execution was not demonstrated with default Content Security Policy settings. The advisory states that no confidentiality, integrity, or availability impact was identified, while its structured scoring metadata separately assigns low integrity impact. Sites that disable or relax the default CSP have increased exposure. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.1.8, 2026.6.3, 2026.7.2, and 2026.8.0.

advisories.title: Discourse: Reject literal backslash path separators in iframe src traversal guard
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.1.8, 2026.6.3, 2026.7.2, and 2026.8.0, the iframe src traversal guard did not treat literal backslashes as path separators after decoded dot segments. A crafted source could therefore pass an allowed_iframes subpath check while browser URL normalization moved the iframe outside the intended allowed path. The resulting iframe could load content from a location that the administrator did not allow. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.1.8, 2026.6.3, 2026.7.2, and 2026.8.0.

advisories.title: Discourse: Wildcard iframe origin allowlist bypass via authority separators
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.1.8, 2026.6.3, 2026.7.2, and 2026.8.0, sites using wildcard patterns in the allowed_iframes setting could accept a crafted iframe URL whose allowlisted suffix appeared after a URL authority separator. The wildcard origin check matched the allowed domain text, while browser URL parsing selected a different attacker-controlled origin. A user with posting privileges could exploit the flaw through a post or a Onebox oEmbed response and cause an attacker-controlled iframe to be rendered independently of the allowlisted domain. Successful exploitation requires a site-configured wildcard iframe pattern and the ability to create a post or trigger an oEmbed request for an attacker-controlled URL. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.1.8, 2026.6.3, 2026.7.2, and 2026.8.0.

advisories.title: Discourse: Encode action_code_who in mention URLs
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.1.8, 2026.6.3, 2026.7.2, and 2026.8.0, the topic small-action and nested-activity-log components interpolated the free-form action_code_who value into mention-link href attributes without URL encoding. A quote-bearing display name could terminate the intended URL attribute and inject attacker-controlled elements into the trusted rendered markup. Although the visible mention text was escaped, the unencoded path component allowed stored HTML injection when another user viewed the affected topic action or activity log. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.1.8, 2026.6.3, 2026.7.2, and 2026.8.0.

advisories.title: Discourse: Block post iframes whose encoded userinfo bypasses the allowed_iframes allowlist
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.1.8, 2026.6.3, 2026.7.2, and 2026.8.0, the Discourse post sanitizer allowed a stored cross-origin iframe to bypass the allowed_iframes prefix policy when the iframe src contained encoded userinfo. The sanitizer validated a decoded form differently from the stored iframe src, allowing the browser to interpret an attacker-controlled host while the allowlist check accepted the encoded URL as an allowed prefix. An authenticated user with posting privileges could persist the iframe in a post and cause attacker-controlled cross-origin content to be rendered. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.1.8, 2026.6.3, 2026.7.2, and 2026.8.0.

advisories.title: Discourse: Escape LIKE metacharacters in upload paths to prevent disclosure
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.1.8, 2026.6.3, 2026.7.2, and 2026.8.0, authenticated users could supply unescaped SQL LIKE metacharacters to upload-resolution patterns, causing wildcard input to select unrelated upload records instead of matching a literal identifier. The affected upload metadata, URL-lookup, and cooked-video-placeholder paths could resolve uploads the user was not authorized to access. This allowed disclosure of restricted metadata, including original filenames and secure-upload paths, without modifying the upload records. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.1.8, 2026.6.3, 2026.7.2, and 2026.8.0.

advisories.title: Discourse: HTML injection in PrettyText.format_for_email from cooked-attribute reparsing
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.1.7, 2026.6.2, 2026.7.1, and 2026.8.0-latest.1, Discourse has HTML injection in PrettyText.format_for_email because cooked attribute values are reparsed as markup. Crafted Vimeo iframe sources, secure-upload URLs or dimensions, and hashtag data-slug values can cause decoded attribute text to be reinterpreted as HTML. The vulnerable conversion also fails to strictly validate the Vimeo iframe host and path, allowing non-Vimeo allowlisted iframes to be converted. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.1.7, 2026.6.2, 2026.7.1, and 2026.8.0-latest.1.

advisories.title: Discourse: Onebox iframe origin allowlist enforces URL authority boundary
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.1.7, an authenticated user could submit specially formed URLs that bypassed the Onebox allowlist and embedded malicious content in a site. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.1.7, 2026.6.2, 2026.7.1, and 2026.8.0-latest.1.

advisories.title: Discourse: Strip SQL comments and use non-recursive parameter interpolation in Data Explorer
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. From 2026.1.0-latest until 2026.1.7, 2026.6.2, 2026.7.1, and 2026.8.0-latest.1, anyone able to run a parameterized Data Explorer query, including non-staff members of a group a query is shared with, could craft parameter values that escaped the intended query and executed arbitrary SQL through plugins/discourse-data-explorer/lib/discourse_data_explorer/data_explorer.rb and plugins/discourse-data-explorer/lib/discourse_data_explorer/workflows/sql_action/v1.rb. Recursive parameter interpolation allowed one parameter value to introduce another parameter, and parameter declarations in SQL comments could be used to inject a statement. Queries run in a read-only transaction, so data could not be modified, but any table could be read. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.1.7, 2026.6.2, 2026.7.1, and 2026.8.0-latest.1.

advisories.title: Discourse: Stored XSS in staff action logs injects staff UI
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.1.6, the staff action log model rendered unescaped previous and new value fields that could inject stored cross-site scripting into the staff interface. The issue is fixed in 2026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.0.

advisories.title: Discourse: Stored XSS chat-transcript username unescaped in Rich Text Editor
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.0, the Rich Text Editor rendered a chat-transcript username as HTML, allowing stored cross-site scripting. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.0.

advisories.title: Discourse: Templates endpoint exposes hidden tag names
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.0, the discourse_templates endpoint exposed hidden tag names because DiscourseTemplates::TemplatesSerializer in plugins/discourse-templates/app/serializers/discourse_templates/templates_serializer.rb did not filter tags through the request Guardian. The serializer did not respect tag group permissions, allowing users to see tags they were not permitted to view. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.0.

advisories.title: Discourse: Unauthorized eavesdropping on private AI bot conversations.
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.0, an authenticated user could eavesdrop on private AI bot conversations through the AI bot reply stream. The issue is fixed in 2026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.0.

advisories.title: Discourse: Non-participant moderators can read, edit, and delete PM content through Discourse AI reviewables
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.0, Discourse AI reviewables associated with private messages could appear in the moderator review queue of a moderator who was not a participant in the message. Reviewable visibility filtering did not restrict private-message reviewables to the audience permitted to access the underlying private-message topic, allowing the moderator to read otherwise confidential content. Depending on the available reviewable action, the moderator could also modify the private message by closing its topic or deleting a post. Exploitation requires an authenticated moderator account and a pre-existing Discourse AI reviewable associated with a private message. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.0.

advisories.title: Discourse: Duplicate lookup reveals restricted topic titles through canonicalized URLs
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.0, TopicLink.extract_from, TopicLink.ensure_entry_for, and TopicLink.duplicate_lookup do not consistently enforce Guardian.can_see? checks when processing internal links. An authenticated user can submit links to restricted topics, private messages, or hidden posts and receive canonicalized slugs or titles in the composer_messages duplicate_lookup response even though the targets are not visible to that user. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.0.

advisories.title: Discourse: Anonymous sidebar serialization exposes descriptions of category-restricted tags
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.0, SiteSerializer.anonymous_default_navigation_menu_tags serializes tags from SiteSetting.default_navigation_menu_tags without applying DiscourseTagging.filter_visible for the anonymous viewer. An unauthenticated user can retrieve restricted tag names and descriptions through /site.json when those tags are limited by inaccessible categories, category tag groups, or tag-group permissions. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.0.

advisories.title: Discourse: Onebox Domain Blocklist Bypass via Case-Sensitive Comparison
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.0, Onebox::DomainChecker.is_blocked? compares hostnames and SiteSetting.blocked_onebox_domains entries case-sensitively, allowing an attacker to bypass configured Onebox domain restrictions by changing character casing in a redirect target hostname. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.0.

advisories.title: Discourse: Stored XSS in discourse-local-dates plugin
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.0, the discourse-local-dates plugin rendered crafted local-date format data as HTML on sites with a modified or disabled default Content Security Policy. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.0.

advisories.title: Discourse: Stored XSS in the moderation review queue
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.0, a low-privileged user could place crafted content in the moderation review queue that executed stored cross-site scripting when a moderator viewed it on a site with a modified or disabled default Content Security Policy. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.0.

advisories.title: Discourse: Private Chat Threat Message Disclosure via Chat Onebox Channel/Threat ID Mismatch
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.0, plugins/chat/lib/chat/onebox_handler.rb resolves Chat::Thread by route thread_id independently of the route channel_id before checking whether the user can preview the selected chat channel. An authenticated user can pair a public channel ID with a private thread ID in a /onebox.json request and obtain private thread message content. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.0.

advisories.title: Discourse: Review queue exposes flag-related private message excerpts to category group moderators
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.1, on sites with category group moderation enabled, the review queue could include an excerpt (and permalink) of the private message attached to a flag, even when the reviewing category moderator was not a participant in that message. These notify_moderators flag messages are addressed only to moderators and, for core flags, to a category's moderation groups as they existed when the flag was raised, so a category group moderator could read flag-discussion content they were not authorized to see. This affects official plugins that create such messages and core flags raised before a moderator's group was granted moderation of the category. Only the confidentiality of a limited excerpt of these flag-related private messages is affected; no content can be modified or deleted. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.1.

advisories.title: Discourse: Stored XSS via unescaped actor name in post actions
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.7.0, the post action component failed to escape user-controlled display names before interpolating them into an HTML string passed to trustHTML. A user who could choose a crafted display name could persist markup in post action descriptions. Viewing the affected user activity streams could execute attacker-controlled script in another user's browser. This issue is fixed in version 2026.7.0.

advisories.title: Discourse: Shared-draft titles and excerpts leak through group post serialization
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior o 2026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.0, users who were allowed to view a group’s activity, but were not permitted to see shared drafts, could still receive shared-draft entries through the group posts and group mentions endpoints. This could disclose shared-draft topic titles and post excerpt/content, resulting in an information disclosure of unpublished draft material. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.0.

advisories.title: Discourse: Cache poisoning/XSS via color scheme cookies
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.0, an unauthenticated attacker could send a single request with a crafted color_scheme_id (or dark_scheme_id) cookie to inject arbitrary HTML into a Discourse page. Because the cookie value was rendered into a color scheme tag without escaping, the attacker could break out of the attribute and inject a tag that bypassed Discourse's nonce-based Content Security Policy, resulting in arbitrary JavaScript execution in visitors' browsers. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.0.

advisories.title: Discourse: Hidden first-post excerpt is emitted in Q&A schema JSON-LD
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.0, hidden or otherwise unviewable first-post content was leaked as an excerpt in the publicly-served Q&A (QAPage) JSON-LD structured data, exposing it to any unauthenticated visitor and to search-engine crawlers. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.1.6, 2026.5.2, 2026.6.1, and 2026.7.0.

advisories.title: Discourse: Remote code execution via pdf uploads
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.6.0, 2026.5.1, 2026.4.2, and 2026.1.5, under certain non-default configurations, processing of PDF uploads could be exploited to obtain RCE on the server. This issue is patched in 2026.6.0, 2026.5.1, 2026.4.2, and 2026.1.5.

advisories.title: Discourse: Insufficient SVG sanitization logic
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.6.0, 2026.5.1, 2026.4.2, and 2026.1.5, insufficient SVG sanitization in upload and user avatar handling could lead to cross-site scripting when a user visited specific URLs that are not normally part of community browsing. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.6.0, 2026.5.1, 2026.4.2, and 2026.1.5.

advisories.title: Discourse: Forged AWS SNS bounce notifications can disable a targeted user's email (missing TopicArn binding)
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.6.0, 2026.5.1, 2026.4.2, and 2026.1.5, the AWS SES bounce webhook at POST /webhooks/aws verified that SNS messages were signed by Amazon but did not bind them to trusted TopicArn values, allowing any AWS account holder to publish validly signed forged Bounce notifications that revoke a targeted user email. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.6.0, 2026.5.1, 2026.4.2, and 2026.1.5.

advisories.title: Discourse: Hidden post revisions leak through adjacent visible diffs
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.6.0, 2026.5.1, 2026.4.2, and 2026.1.5, post revisions that should be hidden from regular users could be leaked through visible diffs on adjacent revisions serialized by PostRevisionSerializer. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.6.0, 2026.5.1, 2026.4.2, and 2026.1.5.

advisories.title: Discourse: Hidden tag names leaked via category serializers
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.6.0, 2026.5.1, 2026.4.2, and 2026.1.5.

advisories.title: Discourse: Signup-time primary_group_id assignment grants whisperer access
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.6.0, 2026.5.1, 2026.4.2, and 2026.1.5.

advisories.title: Discourse: Stored-XSS in 2FA delete confirmation modal
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.6.0, 2026.5.1, 2026.4.2, and 2026.1.5, a malicious second factor name on an attacker-controlled account was not escaped in the delete confirmation dialog, allowing stored cross-site scripting when an administrator impersonated that account. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.6.0, 2026.5.1, 2026.4.2, and 2026.1.5.

advisories.title: Discourse: Topic featured link susceptible to stored XSS
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to 2026.6.0, 2026.5.1, 2026.4.2, and 2026.1.5, a topic "featured link" was not sufficiently normalized and escaped before being rendered in the topic list, allowing a user who can set a featured link to inject JavaScript when default Content Security Policy protections were modified or disabled. This issue is fixed in versions 2026.6.0, 2026.5.1, 2026.4.2, and 2026.1.5.

advisories.title: libheif: Heap Buffer OOB Read in overlay compositing due to wrong alpha stride
advisories.summary: libheif is a HEIF and AVIF file format decoder and encoder. Versions 1.21.2 and prior contain a heap buffer over-read in HeifPixelImage::overlay() in libheif/pixelimage.cc. When compositing an overlay image (iovl) whose child image has a different bit depth for the alpha channel than for the color channels, the function indexes into the alpha plane using the color channel stride (in_stride) instead of the previously retrieved alpha_stride, causing reads past the end of the alpha buffer (up to 3,123 bytes for a 100×50 image with 10-bit color and 8-bit alpha). A crafted HEIF file can exploit this to cause a denial of service (crash) or potentially disclose adjacent heap memory through leaked bytes embedded in the decoded output pixels. This issue has been fixed in versionThis issue has been fixed in version 1.22.0.

advisories.title: Discourse: Cross-site backup access via path traversal in multisite local backups
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. From versions 2026.1.0-latest to before 2026.1.4, 2026.3.0-latest to before 2026.3.1, and 2026.4.0-latest to before 2026.4.1, a path traversal vulnerability in Discourse backup handling could allow an authenticated administrator on one site in a multisite deployment to access backup files belonging to another site when backups are stored locally. In affected configurations, an admin on Site A could potentially retrieve sensitive backup data from Site B (same host, multisite) by crafting a backup download request with a traversal payload. This issue has been patched in versions 2026.1.4, 2026.3.1, 2026.4.1, and 2026.5.0-latest.1.

advisories.title: Discourse: Replying to a whisper lets non-whisperers create staff-only whisper posts
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. From versions 2026.1.0-latest to before 2026.1.4, 2026.3.0-latest to before 2026.3.1, and 2026.4.0-latest to before 2026.4.1, a flaw in how replies to whisper posts are handled allows authenticated users outside the groups configured in whispers_allowed_groups to post into a topic's staff-only whisper channel. The injected content is visible to whisperers (typically staff) alongside legitimate whispers. Only sites that have whispers enabled are affected. This issue has been patched in versions 2026.1.4, 2026.3.1, 2026.4.1, and 2026.5.0-latest.1.

advisories.title: Discourse: GroupPostSerializer leaks hidden full names through reaction post association
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. From versions 2026.1.0-latest to before 2026.1.4, 2026.3.0-latest to before 2026.3.1, and 2026.4.0-latest to before 2026.4.1, GroupPostSerializer declared include_user_long_name? as the predicate for its :name attribute, but AMS looks for include_name?. The misnamed predicate was never called, so object.user.name was always serialized regardless of SiteSetting.enable_names. This issue has been patched in versions 2026.1.4, 2026.3.1, 2026.4.1, and 2026.5.0-latest.1.

advisories.title: Discourse: Chat misauthorization and information disclosure
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. From versions 2026.1.0-latest to before 2026.1.4, 2026.3.0-latest to before 2026.3.1, and 2026.4.0-latest to before 2026.4.1, four authorization/disclosure issues in the chat plugin (one also involving discourse-calendar): read-only category users could create chat threads, self-deleted chat messages could be restored by their author after channel access was revoked, moderators reviewing a flagged chat message were shown the channel's current last_message (often unrelated DM content), and calendar event payloads exposed the attached chat channel and its last message to viewers without chat access (including anonymous users). This affects sites with the chat plugin enabled; the calendar issue additionally requires discourse-calendar. This issue has been patched in versions 2026.1.4, 2026.3.1, 2026.4.1, and 2026.5.0-latest.1.

advisories.title: Discourse: Public chat MessageBus broadcasts are not restricted to chat-eligible users
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. From versions 2026.1.0-latest to before 2026.1.4, 2026.3.0-latest to before 2026.3.1, and 2026.4.0-latest to before 2026.4.1, chat events for public category channels are published to MessageBus without permission scoping, so any MessageBus subscriber without chat enabled could receive chat message payloads in real time. This issue has been patched in versions 2026.1.4, 2026.3.1, 2026.4.1, and 2026.5.0-latest.1.

advisories.title: Discourse: Bot debug endpoints disclose whisper translation audit logs
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. From versions 2026.1.0-latest to before 2026.1.4, 2026.3.0-latest to before 2026.3.1, and 2026.4.0-latest to before 2026.4.1, bot debug endpoints disclose whisper translation audit logs. This issue has been patched in versions 2026.1.4, 2026.3.1, 2026.4.1, and 2026.5.0-latest.1.

advisories.title: Discourse: Non-staff group owners can see email password in plaintext through group history
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. From versions 2026.1.0-latest to before 2026.1.4, 2026.3.0-latest to before 2026.3.1, and 2026.4.0-latest to before 2026.4.1, group owners who are not necessarily admins or moderators can view a group's outgoing email/SMTP credentials in plaintext via the group history log (/groups/:name/logs.json). Affected fields: email_password, email_username, smtp_server, smtp_port, smtp_ssl_mode. The most sensitive item is the SMTP password, which an owner could use to send mail as the group from outside Discourse. This impacts sites that have configured per-group SMTP credentials and granted group ownership to users who should not have access to those credentials. This issue has been patched in versions 2026.1.4, 2026.3.1, 2026.4.1, and 2026.5.0-latest.1.

advisories.title: Discourse: Don't leak restricted tag group names via tag info
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. From versions 2026.1.0-latest to before 2026.1.4, 2026.3.0-latest to before 2026.3.1, and 2026.4.0-latest to before 2026.4.1, DetailedTagSerializer#tag_group_names returned every tag group a tag belonged to without filtering against the requesting user's visibility. With SiteSetting.tags_listed_by_group enabled, anonymous and unprivileged users hitting TagsController#info (which is exempt from requires_login) could read the names of tag groups restricted to specific user groups or non-visible categories. This issue has been patched in versions 2026.1.4, 2026.3.1, 2026.4.1, and 2026.5.0-latest.1.

advisories.title: Discourse: Hidden reply-to post raw can be disclosed through AI explain prompts
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. From versions 2026.1.0-latest to before 2026.1.4, 2026.3.0-latest to before 2026.3.1, and 2026.4.0-latest to before 2026.4.1, the AI "explain" helper only checks can_see? on the post being explained, not its reply_to_post, so any authenticated user with access to the AI helper could read the raw contents of a hidden parent post by invoking "Explain" on a reply to it. This issue has been patched in versions 2026.1.4, 2026.3.1, 2026.4.1, and 2026.5.0-latest.1.

advisories.title: Discourse: Prevent webhook payload disclosure on event redelivery
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. From versions 2026.1.0-latest to before 2026.1.4, 2026.3.0-latest to before 2026.3.1, and 2026.4.0-latest to before 2026.4.1, the MessageBus.publish call for /web_hook_events/<id> in Jobs::RedeliverWebHookEvents did not pass group_ids, leaving the channel readable by any authenticated user (or anonymous user on instances where login_required is disabled). Webhook IDs are sequential integers and trivially enumerable. This issue has been patched in versions 2026.1.4, 2026.3.1, 2026.4.1, and 2026.5.0-latest.1.

advisories.title: Discourse: Category queue reviewers can read raw incoming emails from queued posts
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. From versions 2026.1.0-latest to before 2026.1.4, 2026.3.0-latest to before 2026.3.1, and 2026.4.0-latest to before 2026.4.1, ReviewableQueuedPostSerializer unconditionally included payload["raw_email"] for posts that arrived via incoming email. Category moderation group members reaching the review queue could therefore read the full inbound email source (headers, sender trace, MUA, body) without being in view_raw_email_allowed_groups - the trust boundary that gates the dedicated raw-email endpoint. This issue has been patched in versions 2026.1.4, 2026.3.1, 2026.4.1, and 2026.5.0-latest.1.

advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. This issue has been fixed in versions 2026.1.4, 2026.3.1, 2026.4.1 and 2026.5.0-latest.1.

advisories.title: Discourse: Information Disclosure in Form Template API Due to Missing Authorization
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Impact is limited to disclosure of site configuration metadata. This issue has been fixed in versions 2026.1.4, 2026.3.1, 2026.4.1 and 2026.5.0-latest.1.

advisories.title: Discourse: Cached outdated summaries can leak removed content
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. This issue has been fixed in versions 2026.1.4, 2026.3.1, 2026.4.1 and 2026.5.0-latest.1. To work around this issue, restrict summary generation by tightening the allowed groups on the summarization Personas.

advisories.title: Discourse: Staged user custom fields are exposed on public invite pages
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. advisories.title: Discourse: Hidden tag visibility bypass on tag routes
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. From versions 2026.1.0-latest to before 2026.1.3, 2026.2.0-latest to before 2026.2.2, and 2026.3.0-latest to before 2026.3.0, a user may be able to purchase a lower tier subscription but grant themselves the benefits that comes along with a higher tier subscription. advisories.title: discourse-subscriptions plugin leaking stripe API key in multisite environment
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. From versions 2026.1.0-latest to before 2026.1.3, 2026.2.0-latest to before 2026.2.2, and 2026.3.0-latest to before 2026.3.0, an authenticated moderator-level user could retrieve post content, topic titles, and usernames from categories they were not authorized to view. advisories.title: Discourse: Authorization bypass in oneboxer via user-controlled category id
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. advisories.title: Discourse: Stored XSS via unescaped assignee name
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. From versions 2026.1.0-latest to before 2026.1.3, 2026.2.0-latest to before 2026.2.2, and 2026.3.0-latest to before 2026.3.0, when the hidden prioritize_full_name_in_ux site setting is enabled (defaults to false, requires console access to change), user and group display names are rendered without HTML escaping in several assignment-related UI paths. This issue has been patched in versions 2026.1.3, 2026.2.2, and 2026.3.0.

advisories.title: Discourse: Category group moderators can perform actions on topics in restricted categories without read access
advisories.summary: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform.
